title: Basic token tracking on message completion
steps: Create an assistant message using createAssistantMessage()
Call finishMessage() with usage data: { tokensIn: 100, tokensOut: 50, cost: 0.005 }
Retrieve the message from database using loadMessages()
expected_result: Message row contains correct token values persisted in database
notes: Core functionality - must work for feature to be viable

title: Handle null/undefined token values gracefully
steps: Call finishMessage() without providing usage parameter
expected_result: Message stores null for all token fields when no usage data provided
notes: Important for backward compatibility and optional token tracking

title: Handle partial usage data (only some fields provided)
steps: Call finishMessage() with partial usage: { tokensIn: 200 }
expected_result: Message stores provided values and null for missing fields
notes: Some providers may not return all token fields

title: Track zero token usage correctly
steps: Call finishMessage() with usage: { tokensIn: 0, tokensOut: 0, cost: 0 }
expected_result: Zero values are preserved (not converted to null)

title: Handle very large token counts
steps: Call finishMessage() with large usage values
Verify all large values are stored and retrieved correctly
Verify no integer overflow or precision loss
expected_result: Large token counts stored accurately without overflow
notes: Edge case for very long conversations or large context windows

title: step-finish event includes token usage data
test_data: StepFinishData with tokens: { input: 150, output: 75, cacheRead: 10 }
steps: Set up event listener for 'step-finish' event
Create a step-finish part with token data
expected_result: step-finish event payload contains correct token data
notes: Critical for real-time UI updates and monitoring

title: Track cache hit tokens (cacheRead and cacheWrite)
preconditions: Database initialized, supports cache token fields
steps: Add a step-finish part with cacheRead and cacheWrite tokens
Verify cache token values persisted correctly
expected_result: Cache token fields are tracked and persisted alongside regular tokens

title: Cost field stores floating-point values correctly
steps: Verify message.cost is close to 0.0123456789 (within epsilon 0.0001)
expected_result: Cost stored with reasonable floating-point precision

title: Token data persists across session reload
test_data: Session with multiple messages containing token data
steps: Create session with 3 messages, each with different token counts
Finish all messages with various usage data
Verify all token values match original data
expected_result: Token data persists correctly across database sessions

title: User messages have null token values
steps: Save a user message using saveUserMessage()
expected_result: User messages do not track tokens (null values)
notes: Tokens only tracked for LLM responses (assistant messages)

title: Multiple step-finish events accumulate token usage
preconditions: Event bus and message tracking operational
test_data: Step 1: 100 tokens in/50 out, Step 2: 200 tokens in/100 out
steps: Emit step-finish event with tokens: { input: 100, output: 50 }
Emit second step-finish event with tokens: { input: 200, output: 100 }
Finish message with total usage: { tokensIn: 300, tokensOut: 150 }
Verify final message has cumulative total
expected_result: Token usage correctly aggregates across multiple steps
notes: Multi-step agent loops require accurate aggregation

title: Concurrent token updates do not corrupt data
steps: Concurrently call finishMessage() on both with different token values
Wait for both operations to complete
Verify msg1 has correct tokens (not mixed with msg2)
Verify msg2 has correct tokens (not mixed with msg1)
expected_result: Token data isolated per message, no race conditions

title: toModelMessages() does not expose token data
preconditions: Messages with token data in database
steps: Create and finish message with token data
Verify returned ModelMessage[] does not include token fields
Verify ModelMessage only contains role, content, etc.
expected_result: Token data is internal metadata, not included in LLM context
notes: Tokens are for tracking, not part of conversation context

title: Reject or handle negative token values
steps: Attempt to call finishMessage() with negative token values
Observe system behavior (error thrown or values clamped to 0)
If stored, retrieve message and check stored values
expected_result: System rejects negative values OR stores as-is for debugging (document behavior)
notes: Edge case - API should never return negative, but validate defensive coding

title: Token data tracked regardless of finish reason
test_data: Different finish reasons: stop, tool-calls, length
steps: Create message and finish with reason='stop', tokens provided
Create message and finish with reason='tool-calls', tokens provided
Create message and finish with reason='length', tokens provided
expected_result: Token usage tracked for all finish reasons
notes: Token consumption happens regardless of why response ended
